correctness.rationale: The published integral complement theorem (Y ≃ VR≤2(D) ≃ S2) and unit boundaries for ten exceptional maximal tetrahedra yield 0→H3(X;Z)→Z[T]→H2(Y;Z)→0. The inclusion VR≤2↪Y is G-equivariant on H2; A5 acts trivially on Z by perfectness and inversion acts by -1 because it fixes no simplex of VR≤2 (Lefschetz number 0 and connected S2 homology). Normalizing each relative generator by its boundary identifies the full relative G-action with δ(g) times tetra permutation, so kernel is exactly the claimed integral twisted augmentation lattice. Rational decomposition follows from the two five-tetra A5-orbits exchanged by inversion. Exact standalone verifier enumerates 3272 faces and all 120 group elements, returns VERIFY_OK; independent mod2 boundary ranks are (1,19,131,409,582,390,100,0) and Betti ranks (0,0,0,9,0,0,0). Finite tests verify finite claims; the integral lattice statement is proved by exact sequence, not extrapolated from mod2.

originality.rationale: The closest same-object published theorem classifies a wedge of nine spheres, not its A5×C2 integral homology action. Its Section 4 provides the ten tetrahedra, orbit data and non-equivariant attaching maps, which are acknowledged and used, but does not calculate the antipodal degree on the reference sphere or state the twisted augmentation lattice. Published published-finding corpus results for aliases, full characters, equivariant homotopy, graph powers and matching parameters do not give the same implication. Novelty is the integral module identification, with a stated residual risk that it may be viewed as a short implicit corollary of the primary proof.
residual_risks: Because arXiv:2302.14388v1 already supplies the ten tetrahedra, G-orbit structure and attaching-map unit property, the new module formula is a relatively short, albeit not stated, equivariant corollary. Experts might treat it as implicitly contained in that proof.
The related 2023 dissertation On Vietoris-Rips Complexes of the 2-Sphere was only inspected at abstract level; its body may contain equivalent group-action observations.
Semantic published-finding corpus and web searches are incomplete; unknown unpublished work and unindexed formulations cannot be ruled out.
The computational verifier confirms all rational character traces but does not substitute for the integral proof, which depends on published integral inputs.

value.rationale: The canonical dodecahedral scale-three Rips complex has an unusually rich nine-dimensional homology. Its rank and homotopy type do not specify a homology action of the full 120-element isometry group. The integral signed augmentation lattice specifies that structure without any semisimplification, yields a primitive invariant Z-class, and rationally splits into one 1-dimensional and two 4-dimensional constituents with antipodal eigenspace ranks five/four. It is a motivated full symmetry invariant of a natural finite metric complex, rather than a parameter-tuned small numerical curiosity; it does not require a broader paper-scale theorem for utility.
